description: Where the Maps screen may look for a known route when a person searches for one. Each source is an Overpass API server, which answers from OpenStreetMap data (Open Database Licence). A search goes to the host of one of these and to no other. The terms of each were read on the day given; see docs/sources.md. Add your own in <data directory>/catalog/routes/route-sources.json.

sources.name: Private.coffee
sources.operator: Private.coffee, a non-profit association in Austria
sources.termsNote: Terms of use dated 10 April 2026: the endpoint may be used in any project that needs OpenStreetMap data, with no registration and no rate limit. They ask users to optimise queries and limit simultaneous requests, to send no personally identifiable information, to credit OpenStreetMap, and to send a meaningful User-Agent with the project's name and a link to it. Not to be used for projects related to warfare, or where incorrect data could cause serious consequences. No warranty; the service may end at any time.

sources.name: dresel.systems, Europe
sources.operator: Christian Dresel, a private person in Germany
sources.termsNote: The operator's page (in German) describes an open server, free for everyone, with no registration and no key, run privately on limited hardware: at most four queries at once from one address, no guarantee of availability, and blocking in case of abuse. Its entry on the OpenStreetMap wiki asks applications to send a User-Agent or Referer that identifies them. Data is refreshed about once a day.

sources.name: dresel.systems, North America
sources.operator: Christian Dresel, a private person in Germany
sources.termsNote: As for the Europe server, which is run by the same person on the same machine. This endpoint was not queried when the terms were read.
